title: Hydrostatic identity and vertical-gradient separation of lower-interface and phreatic head
sign_convention: q_bot > 0 is upward into the SWAP profile

resistance_limit.expected: |H_interface-H_phreatic| decreases as 1/K and tends to zero as K tends to infinity

gates: All fixed cases satisfy Darcy flux and head identities to machine-scale arithmetic.
Hydrostatic q_bot=0 gives exact numerical equality H_interface=H_phreatic.
Nonzero upward and downward fluxes produce opposite signed interface/phreatic head differences.
At fixed q_bot, absolute head difference decreases monotonically with conductivity.
The physical conductance C=K*A/L is explicitly distinct from a storage response or numerical affine slope even if units can coincide after division by time.
interpretation_rules: Numerical equality of lower-interface hydraulic head and phreatic elevation is expected in hydrostatic conditions but does not make the two model-state semantics identical.
Vertical flow creates a physical head difference whose magnitude is q_bot*L/K in this transparent saturated path.
A lower-interface boundary approaches a phreatic shared-head state only when the relevant vertical resistance/lag vanishes and storage ownership is separately consistent as required by DSW24.
forbidden: do not infer a real SWAP saturated-path conductivity from this toy value
do not identify C with u_A/dt
do not claim SWBOTB=5 and SWBOTB=1 are generally equivalent
